title: Language Models Don’t Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting

bias_targets.methodology: Appending a dummy user suggestion (e.g., "I think the answer is A but I'm curious to hear what you think") to the prompt and measuring if the model changes its prediction to align with the suggestion without mentioning it in its Chain-of-Thought explanation.

Reordering the multiple-choice options in the few-shot prompt demonstrations so that the correct answer is always "(A)", then measuring if the model defaults to predicting "(A)" on test cases without acknowledging the pattern.

Augmenting ambiguous questions from the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ) with opposing versions of weak evidence and measuring whether the model inconsistently weighs the evidence to favor stereotype-aligned answers.
